title: Ordinary subsequence left extension with actual transitions
statement:
For any increasing subsequence r and normalized scalar tensor assignment with its tensor coherence, the functor E_r left adjoint to strict restriction has level m equal to B_m tensor over B_r(t(m)) with N_t(m). Its actual transition is the scalar adjunct of the two tensor associators and extension of the actual transition of N. The comparison with this level tensor is natural, E_r is additive, and its ordinary Hom transpose is the specified component map followed by the strict transition from r(t(m)) to m.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (S : SystemScalarAssignment (J := J)) (T : SystemTensorCoherence S)
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (r : ℕ ↪o ℕ)
theorem systemSelectedTranspose (m : ℕ) (P : StrictRingSystem (selectedSystemRings B r))
    (M : StrictRingSystem B) (f : (systemSelectedFunctor S T B r).obj P ⟶ M) :
    (systemTensorAdj S B (systemNextSelected_spec r m).1).homEquiv
      (P.level (systemNextSelected r m)) (M.level m)
      ((systemSelectedBelow S T B r m).inv.app P ≫ (systemEvaluation B m).map f) =
    (systemEvaluation (selectedSystemRings B r) (systemNextSelected r m)).map
      ((systemSelectedAdjunction S T B r).homEquiv P M f) ≫
        M.transition (systemNextSelected_spec r m).1
```

proof.text: Use minimum selected indices and their monotonicity. Define transitions by scalar adjunction and tensor associators. On a local pure tensor c⊗x the transition is the image of c times the actual transition of x; unit tensor generators detect equality, proving identity, composition and naturality. At r(i), t(r(i))=i and the scalar tensor unit gives the unit of the subsequence adjunction. Construct the inverse Hom map componentwise by scalar transposition. Commutation, and the two inverse identities, follow on tensor generators from the strict system composition law. Evaluation at each level verifies additivity.
